chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ: إِنِّي قَدْ أَشْفَقْتُ مِنْ دُعَاءِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَلَى يَقْطِينَ وَمَا وَلَدَ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا الْحَسَنِ لَيْسَ حَيْثُ تَذْهَبُ، إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُ فِي صَلْبِ الْكَافِرِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْحِصَاةِ فِي اللَّبَنَةِ يَجِيءُ الْمَطَرُ فَيَغْسِلُ اللَّبَنَةَ وَلَا يُضِرُّ الْحِصَاةَ شَيْئًا

translations.en: I said to him: I am fearful because of the supplication of Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) against Yaqtin and his offspring, so he said: O Abu al-Hasan, it is not as you think; verily the believer in the back-bone of the disbeliever is like the stone in the clay brick; when the rain comes it washes the clay but does not harm the stone in any way.

en.summary: This hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) addresses the Shia concept of individual accountability (istiqra') by clarifying that a believer's spiritual state is not negated by their disbelieving parent's status. The metaphor of the stone within the clay brick illustrates that while the parent's faith may be washed away like the clay, the child's faith remains intact and distinct, a key principle in distinguishing between familial lineage and personal piety.
en.seo_question: How does the faith of a believer affect their status if their parent or ancestor was a disbeliever?
